column1: # Test run policy table (issue #407 item 3) — single source of truth for
# per-class QEMU run policy. Consumed ONLY via tools/test-policy.awk
# (tools/meson/qemu_test.py + scripts/run_all_classes.sh); never parsed
# anywhere else. `|` separator survives editors/formatters (no TABs).
# Format: scope|selector|key|value   (`#` lines are comments)
# Tiers, lowest precedence first (later line wins within a tier):
#   default < group < arch < class
# An arch record beats a group record (riscv64 always 400 s, even heavy).
# Keys: expect_timeout, outer_timeout, max_attempts, stall_signatures,
#   watchdog_stall, expected_panic, expected_empty, arch_scope, build_scope.
# `members` rows are resolver metadata (group membership), not policy.
# Each row carries its originating issue as provenance.
# Reserved: `requires|ovmf` key for q35 OVMF guards (deferred follow-up).
default|*|expect_timeout|120
default|*|outer_timeout|600
default|*|max_attempts|2
default|*|stall_signatures|TIMEOUT,QEMU_EXIT
default|*|watchdog_stall|220
default|*|expected_panic|0
default|*|expected_empty|0
default|*|arch_scope|any
default|*|build_scope|any
# scope_cause: WHY the arch_scope is what it is (shown by run_all_classes.sh
# on exclusion). Vocabulary: common (runs everywhere listed — the vast
# majority), hole (should run but can't yet — work item with issue ref),
# unsupported (the arch lacks the function — permanent; pendant named
# where one exists), special-arch (one arch only, by design — documented
# here, enforced by list membership, not scope).
default|*|scope_cause|common: no arch restriction
class|smp|scope_cause|hole: PSCI/HSM test bodies missing on aarch64+riscv64, see #525
class|smp_multicpu|scope_cause|hole: PSCI/HSM test bodies missing on aarch64+riscv64, see #525
class|ahci_live|scope_cause|unsupported: no Q35/ICH9 off-x86 (pendant: virtio-blk via storage class)
class|iommu_live|scope_cause|unsupported: no VT-d off-x86 (pendant: SMMUv3 pending, see #168)
arch|riscv64|expect_timeout|400
arch|riscv64|outer_timeout|1200
group|heavy|members|core_basic core_sync core_sched core_task core_memory core_syscall core_tracing smp_multicpu ahci_live iommu_live deadline
group|heavy|expect_timeout|250
class|testrunner|expected_panic|1
class|lockpark_tripwire|expected_panic|1
class|task_fpu|expected_empty|1
class|smp|arch_scope|x86_64
class|smp_multicpu|arch_scope|x86_64
class|smp_waitpid|arch_scope|x86_64
class|ahci_live|arch_scope|x86_64
class|iommu_live|arch_scope|x86_64
class|ahci_live|build_scope|debug
class|iommu_live|build_scope|debug
# (2026-11-22) #605 re-test: capability runs 200 tests, ~80 per 120 s wall on
# nexios-qe TCG (serial 20:43, verdict 20:45:43) => ~300 s full class. Per-class
# rows from measured wall-clock seconds.
class|capability|expect_timeout|400
class|capability|outer_timeout|900
# (2026-11-24) #592: hal acpi-scan silent stretch (map_page WARN flood ~34KB
# with no S-lines, then silent scan_dmar walk, minutes) exceeds the 120 s
# expect budget — harness kills a slow-but-healthy guest (mid-WARN-line
# kills observed). Raised to cover the worst observed silent stretch.
class|hal|expect_timeout|600
class|hal|outer_timeout|1200
# F11 D6: proc_elf hangs in release ON (x86_64 release STALL 247s even with
# per-test guards — the 135-test aggregate has multiple hang sources). The
# release gate runs proc_elf in debug ON only; release is debug-only.
class|proc_elf|build_scope|debug
# (2026-10-26) The 43 measured+30pct class rows were REMOVED: their values
# were computed in MILLISECONDS from guest TIME rows but this field is
# consumed in SECONDS (run-test.exp `set timeout`, GNU outer `timeout`,
# meson test() timeouts) - e.g. 15022 meant 4.2 hours, not +30pct. Verified
# by units audit: defaults 120/250/400 only make sense as seconds (a 120ms
# QEMU expect gate could never boot), and the aarch64 testrunner 123s
# EXPECTED_PANIC_PASS equals the 120s default firing. Impact was bounded in
# practice by the host watchdog (220s stall preemption), but every failure
# path paid ~220s instead of the intended budget.
# The arch-qualified class-selector MECHANISM (awk) is retained and valid;
# re-add per-class rows ONLY from measured wall-clock SECONDS (boot +
# suite, not guest TIME_ELAPSED), with the wall source cited per row.
# Until then the tier defaults (120 / 250 heavy / 400 riscv64) apply.
